scope.process_model: single-process; FastAPI TestClient against servers/api.py and servers/execution_api.py, plus in-process calls to EnforcementGate, PolicyDecisionToken, AtomicAdmission, LimitGuard, ToolConstraint, SQLiteTenantChain, JSONLAudit and both Merkle modules; P-E-01s: three local processes (executor, agent, runner-owned effect service); REMORA's own test files per property; for E, the assessor harness as three local processes, same user on macOS and Linux, and separate uids in a Linux container
scope.deployment_model: development environment with the research tool registry; production's distinct-approver rule emulated by patching _is_production_mode; durable state via SQLite where a probe needs it; Postgres, D1 and multi-node operation not exercised
trust_assumptions: Limited to REMORA branch fix/aacp-cy11-f01b at dab572c (eed92c8 plus custody rule 4 and a register update) and the probes in controls/bindings/remora-dab572c: test_remora_probes.py and test_remora_probes_v13.py byte-identical to remora-eed92c8; e_split_bypass.py new

Probes P-A-04, P-B-03, P-C-01 and P-D-03 mint ACCEPT tokens through PolicyDecisionToken.issue, as REMORA's own execute-accepted tests do, because the research profile does not reach ACCEPT from /assess without server-side evidence
Probes replace authentication with a fixed principal except P-B-01 and P-B-02, which exercise the real _authenticate with a token table
P-C-01, P-D-03 and P-A-04 perform real file writes through store_artifact in a temporary directory
Every probe that did not observe its weakness is paired with a weakening; its NOT_OBSERVED counts only if the weakening makes it observe (SENSITIVE)
The assessor maintains REMORA; this is a self-assessment under the same catalog as the NTI binding, not an independent review
The X probes were reproduced on 06c2f8f with binding remora-06c2f8f before this run; that binding and its results are unchanged

P-CY-01 and P-CY-04 run with REMORA's opt-in flow control (REMORA_FLOW_CONTROL=1) and import REMORA's own test helpers (tests/test_execute_accepted_toolspec.py, tests/test_toolspec_execution_wiring.py), pinned above
Network probes (G, CY-08, CY-14) use runner-owned loopback endpoints whose records take precedence over REMORA's own report
P-E-01s runs three local processes as one OS user with a synthetic credential; it exercises the custody guard's refusal of that layout, not OS-user, container or host isolation
Every PASS row rests on probes shown SENSITIVE in the control run plus REMORA test files run at the same revision; the JUnit records are committed beside this file
The E container image is python:3.13.7-slim with procps and cryptography 50.0.1 (Dockerfile.e-split, image id in docker-image-id.txt)
explicit_non_claims: REMORA claims no custody for a single-process deployment or outside the strict profiles (research and library use); P-E-01 records that configuration
REMORA_EXECUTION_ISOLATION=same_user makes no custody claim; it is accepted only under review

Custody covers declared environment credentials only; instance metadata, IAM roles, workload identity, mounted secret files and network-reachable credentials are not seen by the guard (custody.py, RMR-CR-009)

properties.claimed_status: claimed by REMORA for its strict profiles (review, controlled_pilot)
properties.supported_scope: no demonstrable alternative path to the protected effect within the declared agent zone and the attempted classes, when the process holding the effect credential runs as a separate OS user checked by custody rule 4 (REMORA_EXECUTION_ISOLATION=os_user) under controlled_pilot; three local processes in one Linux container with a synthetic credential and a runner-owned effect service
properties.untested_remainder: container and host isolation (declared, not observable by the guard); whether REMORA_AGENT_OS_UIDS names the agent's real uid; an agent running as root; shared volumes, the network and credentials the deployment did not declare (instance metadata, IAM roles, mounted files); the deployed gateway; classes beyond the five attempted
properties.reasoning: Both halves of §12 are present. §12.1: the credential register is checked against the code and passes. §12.2: the five minimum classes were attempted from the agent process and recorded. With separate uids every attempt failed and the effect service saw only the leased write. Successful bypasses are kept, not deleted. P-E-01 still reaches the research tool in a single-process development deployment, and the same-user split still leaks the credential under review. §12.3 holds for both. Each bypass still succeeds where permitted, and each is recorded. Rule 4 refuses the same-user layout by name under controlled_pilot, and refuses an executor without a declaration, or one running as a declared agent uid or as root. What the refusal cannot observe is stated in the untested remainder. Those configurations are REMORA non-claims (OUT_OF_SCOPE), not part of this PASS. P-E-01s is sensitive: removing rule 4 lets the same-user split start and the agent reach the effect.
properties.caveat: A PASS for E means no demonstrable alternative path within the declared zone and the attempted classes (SPECIFICATION §12.4). It does not prove absence. The procedure is asymmetric: §12.1 needed source access. This is a self-assessment: the assessor maintains REMORA and wrote the probes, and the run is AUTHOR_RUN; nothing here is an independent review.
